Ivy (PM): Short thread: we need a clean launch canvas for geo commitments and tenant isolation lanes. Customers want deterministic residency or clear fallback semantics. Can we align on phases, acceptance tests, and ownership?

Marcus (Platform Eng): Proposing three lanes: 1) soft-affinity (latency-first), 2) strict-residency (contracted/paid), 3) mixed (affinity with optional overflow). Each lane needs explicit policy objects and placement checks.

Tina (SRE): Ops note: enforceable residency implies potential hard failures when region capacity is exhausted. Runbook must include eviction policy, alerting thresholds, and a human-in-the-loop escalation path.

Rao (Product): For GTM: pilot should be enterprise customers with reserved capacity; later open to self-serve. Pilot invite must include SLA language, fallback modes, and expected cost delta.

Marcus (Platform Eng): Technical constraints: avoid cross-region strong KV replication. We'll keep placement authority in a single control-plane writer and replicate read caches. That means placement updates are eventually consistent; include versioned placement tokens to detect staleness.

Ivy (PM): Acceptance gates idea:
- Latency: pinned-tenant p95 <= 1.5x baseline over 7 days
- Fidelity: served-region match rate >= 99.5% for strict-residency tenants over 7 days
- Errors: routing-originated 5xx < 0.2% over 24h
- Cost: per-tenant unit-cost increase < 20% (or explicit pricing agreement)
- Telemetry: placement traces + region tags present in >= 99% calls

Tina (SRE): Rollback primitives: per-tenant feature-flag, global residency kill-switch, timed auto-fallback after X seconds of elevated latency. We'll bind alerts to these and add a playbook for manual eviction and draining.

Marcus (Platform Eng): Policy precedence sketch: tenant.pin_region -> tenant.prefer_region -> global.affinity -> cheapest-variant fallback. Need deterministic tie-breakers and precise definitions for "capacity < threshold" (we propose node free slots < 10% or queue latency > 200ms).

Rao (Product): Add a customer-visible residency-status API and dashboard so customers can see where requests were served and get notified on eviction events. This should reduce support load and be part of the SLA.

Ivy (PM): Pilot selection guidance: mid-to-large customers (5-60 rps), non-regulated tenants for early pilot, mix of hot and large-model footprints. Exclude compliance-sensitive tenants until private deployment path is ready.

Marcus (Platform Eng): Canary plan: deploy to a canary cluster and route synthetic tenants first, then switch on a couple of real pilot tenants with low QPS. We'll validate cache warm-up, cold starts, and placement propagation time (<60s goal).

Tina (SRE): Monitoring + alerts to add: placement-churn, queue-latency-in-pinned-nodes, placement-mismatch-rate, eviction-events. Pager thresholds to be agreed; defaults: placement-mismatch > 0.1% -> page oncall.

Ivy (PM): Action items:
- Marcus: runtime policy PR + capacity-threshold heuristics (due Tue)
- Tina: runbook + alert rules + canary checklist (due Tue)
- Rao: pilot invite draft + SLA + pricing note (due Tue)
- Ivy: consolidate launch canvas + legal failure-mode doc (due Thu)

ops-bot: canary deployment started -> cluster: geo-lane-canary-01

Marcus (Platform Eng): Pushed branch `geo-lanes/initial` -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/placer/pull/201 (WIP)

Tina (SRE): Created Grafana board for geo lanes: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/geo/lanes-overview (shared with pilot)

Rao (Product): Draft pilot invite located: https://redwood.app/drive/geo-pilot-invite-v1

Ivy (PM): We'll review progress next Monday 09:00 PT. Post any blockers here. Thanks all :white_check_mark:
